scope: src/main.js lines 21350-23410 — gun-bash/execution choreography, companion operator + FPV drone, HUD (main + split + slot), hit markers, money/killfeed, grenades/smoke/flash projectiles + explosion FX. Cross-checked enemy.takeDamage (7872), barrel explosion (33150), trail updater (44272), maxHp/perks (35952/31066), config keymaps (28621/29611).

findings.title: Explosion corona disc is never billboarded — the blast's brightest element is edge-on / invisible from most angles
findings.description: spawnExplosionFx builds the bright additive corona as a flat PlaneGeometry(2,2) at corona.position.copy(pos) with the default world orientation (facing +Z). It is pushed into G.trails as {isFlash:true} WITHOUT faceCameraBillboard:true and is never passed through _orientVfxBillboard. The trail updater (line 44277) only re-orients a flash plane when faceCameraBillboard is set, so the corona stays world-axis-aligned. Whenever the player isn't looking roughly along ±Z, the corona renders edge-on (a thin sliver) or back-facing — so the single biggest visual punch of a grenade blast is usually invisible. Every other corona/flash in the file (e.g. muzzle corona line 24341, impact ring line 24064-24066) is correctly billboarded.
findings.evidence: const corona=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.PlaneGeometry(2.0,2.0),coronaM); corona.position.copy(pos); scene.add(corona); G.trails.push({mesh:corona,mat:coronaM,timer:.20,maxTime:.20,isFlash:true});  // no faceCameraBillboard, no _orientVfxBillboard
findings.fix: Add faceCameraBillboard:true to the corona trail entry and orient it once at spawn: after `corona.position.copy(pos);` add `_orientVfxBillboard(corona,camera,Math.random()*Math.PI);` and change the push to `G.trails.push({mesh:corona,mat:coronaM,timer:.20,maxTime:.20,isFlash:true,faceCameraBillboard:true,growRate:6});` so it always faces the camera (matching the muzzle corona at 24341).
findings.risk: Negligible. Reuses existing billboard helper and the same per-frame path used by every other flash. No save/perf/state impact; only makes an already-spawned mesh visible from all angles. Slightly larger apparent flash, which is the intent.

findings.title: Main HUD health bar width and color thresholds use raw HP, not HP/maxHp — bar overflows and mis-colors with the extraHp perk / health powerup
findings.description: hudUpdate sets the HP fill as `width = round(P.hp) + '%'` and picks bar color from raw `h` (h>60 green / h>30 amber). #hp-fill is a percentage-width child of the fixed 180px #hp-bar. With the extraHp perk P.maxHp=125 (line 35952/31066) and the +50 health powerup pushes P.hp up to maxHp+50 (line 33075), so at full health the fill is width:125% and overflows the track, and the bar stays green until raw HP < 60 (=48% of max) instead of at a true fraction. The split-screen HUD does this correctly — hudUpdateSlot line 22524 uses min(100,(hp/maxHp)*100) and the co-op p1/p2 bars at 22598 do the same — so the single-player main bar is the inconsistent one.
findings.fix: Mirror the split-HUD math: `const ratio=(P.hp||0)/Math.max(1,P.maxHp||100); const pct=Math.min(100,ratio*100); _hudSetText('hp-val',h); _hudSetStyle('hp-fill','width',pct.toFixed(1)+'%'); _hudSetStyle('hp-fill','background',ratio>.6?'#4cff88':ratio>.3?'#ffcc44':'#ff4444');` (keep the numeric readout as raw h).
findings.risk: Low. Cosmetic-only; no save format change. Only behaviour change is the bar no longer overflowing and the color thresholds becoming fraction-based, which is the intended/standard behaviour and already used by the split HUD.

findings.title: Player grenade kills skip P.kills++, killfeed and combo — every other kill source credits them; grenade kills are 'silent'
findings.description: explodeGrenade, on a lethal blast, calls only addBlood + awardKillMoney + cinematicKill + checkZoneClears. It does NOT increment P.kills, push a killFeed entry, or call comboKill. Every other lethal path does the full set: gun (26448-26451), gun-bash (21433), knife throw (20162-20165), ricochet (25237-25239), dropkick (27662-27666), takedown (36620-36623), and even the explosive-barrel path whose comment literally says 'same as grenade explosion' actually does more — line 33162: `killFeed(false,{dist:d});P.kills++;comboKill(...);P.money+=20`. Net effect: frag-grenade multi-kills don't count toward the run kill stat, never appear in the killfeed (player can't tell the grenade got the kills), and break the player's combo chain instead of extending it.
findings.evidence: if(killed){ addBlood(e.group.position.clone(),false); awardKillMoney(e,false); cinematicKill(e.group.position.clone()); setTimeout(()=>checkZoneClears(),60); }  // no P.kills++, no killFeed, no comboKill
findings.fix: Inside the `if(killed)` block add the canonical trio used by the barrel path: `P.kills++; killFeed(false,{dist:d}); comboKill(false,{source:'grenade-kill',closeRange:THREE.MathUtils.clamp(1-d/5,0,1)}); applyStoryMomentumShock(e,pos,{source:'grenade-kill'});` (d is already computed in the loop).
findings.risk: Low. Adds stat/feed/combo credit that the rest of the game already grants. comboKill on a multi-kill could chain a large combo — desired for frag clears. No save-compat concern.

findings.title: Enemy-thrown (demolitions) grenades route through explodeGrenade and friendly-fire other enemies, awarding the player money/kills
findings.description: spawnEnemyGrenade pushes a projectile with fromEnemy:true (thrown by 'demolitions' enemies, line 11694, aimed at the player's cover). updateGrenades detonates ALL non-smoke/non-flash grenades — including fromEnemy ones — through explodeGrenade(). explodeGrenade has no source check: it damages every enemy in radius and, on kill, calls awardKillMoney(e,false) + cinematicKill, plus self-damages the player. So an enemy frag that lands near other guards damages/kills them and silently pays the player money (and triggers a cinematic kill flash) for kills the player did not make.
findings.evidence: } else { explodeGrenade(explosionPos); spawnExplosionFx(explosionPos); }  // reached for k.fromEnemy===true too; explodeGrenade loops all enemies and calls awardKillMoney(e,false) on any kill
findings.fix: Either (a) pass the source into explodeGrenade and skip awardKillMoney/cinematicKill when fromEnemy (still allow damage if friendly-fire is intended), or (b) gate enemy-killed-by-enemy credit: in explodeGrenade add a `byPlayer` param defaulting true and only run awardKillMoney/cinematicKill when byPlayer; call `explodeGrenade(explosionPos,!k.fromEnemy)`. Simplest surgical change: in updateGrenades pass the flag and guard the award block.
findings.risk: Low–medium. Must not change damage-to-player behaviour. If enemy-grenade enemy-on-enemy damage is intended, keep the damage and only suppress player credit. Verify demolitions encounter balance after the change.

findings.title: Grenade multi-kill spawns N overlapping money popups at the same screen anchor and N stacked money SFX in one frame
findings.description: explodeGrenade can kill several enemies in a single blast; each kill calls awardKillMoney, which appends a moneyPopup div (all positioned identically at right:34px) and fires sfxMoney() (two oscillators each). On a 4-5 kill frag, several '+$xx' labels overlay each other at the same anchor (looks like one number) and 8-10 oscillators start simultaneously, producing a loud clipped money chime. awardKillMoney also calls hudUpdate() once per kill (cheap due to HUD cache, but redundant).
findings.evidence: if(killed){ ... awardKillMoney(e,false); ... }  // awardKillMoney: moneyPopup(total,...); sfxMoney(); hudUpdate(); called per enemy in the radius loop
findings.fix: Accumulate grenade kill money in the loop and emit a single consolidated moneyPopup/sfxMoney after the loop (e.g. tally `grenadeMoney` and `grenadeKills`, then one `moneyPopup(grenadeMoney, kills>1?('x'+kills):'') + sfxMoney() + hudUpdate()`). Or stagger popup vertical offset by kill index. Low priority polish.
findings.risk: Very low. Audio/visual polish only. Ensure single hudUpdate still reflects final money.

findings.title: deploySmoke leaks the base cloud material (cloudM) — only the 24 clones are disposed
findings.description: deploySmoke creates a base MeshBasicMaterial `cloudM`, then clones it 24 times (m=cloudM.clone()) for the billboards. Each clone is pushed into G.trails and disposed by _disposeTrail when its timer expires. The original cloudM is never added to the scene and never disposed, so one MeshBasicMaterial is orphaned per smoke deployment. The shared texture (_vfxDustPuffTex) is safe because clones lack atlasOwnedMap so _disposeTrail won't dispose the shared map.
findings.evidence: const cloudM=new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({map:_vfxDustPuffTex,...}); for(let i=0;i<24;i++){ const m=cloudM.clone(); ... G.trails.push({mesh:b,mat:m,...}); }  // cloudM itself never disposed
findings.fix: Either dispose the base after cloning (`cloudM.dispose();` after the loop — clones already own their own GPU material; disposing the un-uploaded base is safe), or build per-billboard materials inline without a base. Single MeshBasicMaterial per smoke is tiny, so low priority.
findings.risk: Very low. cloudM is never rendered, so disposing it post-loop cannot affect visuals. Do not dispose its .map (shared texture).

findings.title: Gun-bash impact dereferences h.object.userData.enemy without a null/dead guard (drone-fire path guards it)
findings.description: _resolvePistolWhipImpact takes the first raycast hit and immediately does `const enemy=h.object.userData.enemy; enemy.lastPlayerDir.set(...)` with no check that enemy exists or is alive. In practice every mesh returned by EnemyManager.getMeshes() has userData.enemy set (bMesh/hMesh line 6401/6414, limb proxies line 7450), so this does not currently throw, and takeDamage() self-guards dead enemies. But it is the only ray-hit consumer in this region without the defensive guard the drone-fire path uses (line 22238: `const enemy=h.object&&h.object.userData&&h.object.userData.enemy; if(enemy&&!enemy.dead){...}`). Any future mesh added to getMeshes() without userData.enemy would crash here.
findings.fix: Guard the block: `const enemy=h.object&&h.object.userData&&h.object.userData.enemy; if(enemy&&!enemy.dead){ enemy.lastPlayerDir.set(...); ... }` matching the drone-fire pattern. Defensive only.
findings.risk: Very low; pure hardening. No behaviour change today.

findings.title: KeyF focus toggle has no e.repeat guard — holding F rapidly flip-flops focus mode on key auto-repeat
findings.description: KeyF is overloaded: pickup (22398, returns), open door (22399, returns), and otherwise toggleFocus (22421). The focus branch lacks an `!e.repeat` guard, so holding F (when not near a pickup/door) fires keydown repeatedly and toggleFocus() flips P.focusActive on every auto-repeat event, strobing focus mode on/off. Other tap actions in the same handler that should fire once correctly guard with !e.repeat (e.g. Space jump 22393, dodge logic, KeyT takedown 22422). Focus is bound as the 'F' key in both the help legend (28621) and keymap (29611 focus:'KeyF'), confirming it's meant as a tap toggle.
findings.risk: Very low. Prevents an unintended strobe; no other code depends on repeat-firing toggleFocus.

findings.title: _companionLightAction restore captures already-dimmed intensity if it overlaps its own restore window (currently shielded by the 8.5s rate limit)
findings.description: _companionLightAction snapshots current light intensities, dims them to *0.18, and schedules a 1.6s restore. If it ran again before that 1.6s elapsed, clearTimeout cancels the pending restore and the fresh `saved` snapshot captures the already-dimmed 0.18*orig as the 'restore' target — permanently darkening those lights (and dimming further to 0.0324*orig). Today this cannot fire because the command is gated by _companionRate('light',8500) (line 21852), so the 8.5s cooldown always exceeds the 1.6s restore window. It is a latent desync that breaks the moment the cooldown is lowered below 1.6s.
findings.evidence: const saved=lights.map(L=>({L,intensity:L.intensity})); for(const L of saved)L.L.intensity=(L.intensity||1)*.18; COMPANION_ROOM.lightRestore=setTimeout(()=>{for(const s of saved){if(s.L)s.L.intensity=s.intensity;}},1600);
findings.fix: Restore immediately before re-dimming, or store baseline per-light: e.g. keep a Map of original intensities keyed by light and only snapshot when not already dimmed (`if(COMPANION_ROOM.lightRestore){ run-the-pending-restore-now } then snapshot`). Or set restore to the cached original rather than the current value.
findings.risk: Very low today (unreachable due to rate limit). Harden only if the light cooldown is ever reduced.

findings.title: Explosion sparks are low-poly SphereGeometry blobs instead of the textured additive spark quads used by the rest of the VFX
findings.description: spawnExplosionFx scatters 18 sparks as MeshBasicMaterial spheres (SphereGeometry(.06,5,4)). They read as faceted orange dots rather than streaky embers. Elsewhere the game uses billboarded textured spark quads (e.g. line 29934 sparksAtlasQuad with _softRadialTex, billboardRoll, drag/gravity) which look far more 'AAA'. Swapping the explosion sparks to the same soft-radial additive billboards (with motion blur from billboardRollSpeed + drag) would noticeably upgrade the grenade blast that the player sees constantly.
findings.fix: Replace the sphere spark with a small PlaneGeometry using _softRadialTex (additive), set faceCameraBillboard:true, billboardRoll/billboardRollSpeed, drag:.88 and gravity, mirroring the muzzle/impact spark pattern at lines 29934/24285. Keep count/timer the same to preserve perf budget.
findings.risk: Low. Same trail category (isParticle) and lifetime; uses an already-loaded shared texture. Verify _trailBudget particle cap isn't exceeded (count unchanged at 18).
